name: AI scribes & documentation
blurb: Ambient listening, dictation and note-drafting tools. For the ED, the questions that matter most: can it hold several open encounters at once, survive interruptions, filter a loud room, and put text into the right ED note sections?

name: Clinical Q&A & decision support
blurb: Tools that answer clinical questions from the literature with citations. For the ED: speed at the bedside, citation quality, and whether PHI can be entered under a BAA.

name: ECG & cardiac AI
blurb: AI interpretation of 12-lead ECGs, handheld ECG devices and AI stethoscopes. For the ED: OMI/STEMI-equivalent detection, how alerts reach the right person, and FDA status.

name: Imaging triage
blurb: FDA-cleared computer-assisted triage and notification (CADt) software that flags suspected critical findings (ICH, LVO, PE, pneumothorax, fractures) on CT and X-ray. Usually bought by the health system, not individual clinicians.

name: POCUS AI
blurb: Point-of-care ultrasound devices and software with AI guidance, auto-measurement or image-quality feedback. For the ED: speed in resus, glove-friendly use, and what actually needs a paid subscription.

name: Sepsis, triage & early warning
blurb: Risk models for sepsis, deterioration and triage acuity, plus dispatch-level recognition tools. For the ED: published external validation, alert burden, and lead time over clinicians.

name: Discharge & patient follow-up
blurb: Tools that draft discharge instructions and work or school notes, or follow up with patients after discharge. For the ED: reading level, translation, return precautions, and mandatory clinician review.
